title: The Audit Plane
summary: SHEET 13/14, C's one full-red sheet, built on the same sheet metric as every other C sheet. The four-layer assembly from FIG. 4.1 is redrawn in paper lines, and the installed plane becomes the AUDIT PLANE: a paper plane under the whole stack, printed in red with the plan of every layer. The note says 'one diagnostic maps the architecture underneath your pipeline' and the drawing shows exactly that. One leader carries the plane across the divider into the paper audit door on the same row, so drawing and action read as one thing.

reference.borrowed: A CTA band drawn like a construction sheet. A thin ruled frame has '+' crosshairs at chosen corners, faint construction lines continue past the frame, and a vertical rule splits it into a wide statement cell (bold sentence plus muted sentence, then a filled and an outlined button side by side) and a narrow offer cell. It reads as cells inside a ruled frame, not a floating card.
reference.kelwin: The frame becomes C's continuous sheet frame in paper --line on full red: the opening rule at y 96, crosshairs at the two top corners, the col 8|9 divider foot and the band. Vercel's vertical rule is that divider. The title cell carries the shared C head: a paper-square caps label 'Sheet 13/14 · Audit request', the 88px wide 'INITIATE THE / SYSTEM AUDIT.' (430, with the light 300 accent in paper 70%) flush bottom-left, and the 48×2 paper rule. The note cell (cols 9–12) holds the 20px lede. Vercel's construction lines become dashed column verticals and 96px row lines through the drawing field. FIG. 13.1 is the exploded iso assembly (L1 Narrative to L4 Intelligence: the corrected three-piece mark extended by one outer step at the same bar and channel proportions, exact 30°, the same geometry as FIG. 4.1, and not labelled as the logo). It has L1–L4 leaders, three dashed projectors, the paper audit plane, an iso dimension along its front edge (callout A → SCOPE) and callout B on the printed plan (→ OUTPUT), both keyed to the spec table. Vercel's filled and outlined buttons become C's door cells stacked on the 96px module: the paper 'C9·R8 · Initiate System Audit ↗' cell on the plane's row, joined to it by the 'Audit plane · L1–L4' leader, and the ruled 'C9·R9 · Talk to the team →' cell under it. The band is the shared C band: L1–L4 legend plus the segmented title block 'Sheet 13/14 | FIG. 13.1 | Rev C | Kelwin/GTM'.

motion: entrance, in drafting order (--ease-inout, no overshoot): the frame verticals and crosshairs fade in (300ms), and the cell rules draw in raster order (40ms stagger). The title fades in, the 48px rule draws, and the mono labels type on at 24ms per character.

the drawing plots by stroke-dashoffset: construction lines fade in, then the four plates plot core-first (L4→L1, 500ms each, 220ms apart, about 0.9–2.0s). The projectors rise and the L1–L4 labels and leaders fade in.

the one orchestrated moment: at 2.1s the paper audit plane drops into its slot under the stack (opacity plus an 8px settle, 400ms), and the red plan of every layer plots across it. Dimension A and callout B appear. The leader then runs from the plane's right vertex across the divider (500ms). As it arrives, the audit door fills with paper (a scaleX wipe, 500ms) and its red label appears. All motion ends by about 3.6s.
ambient: none. Nothing loops on this sheet.

interaction: hovering spec row A or B inverts its lettered key and its callout in the drawing (A also brightens its dimension line). The audit door turns blush and its ↗ moves 2px up-right. The contact cell inverts (paper fill, red text) and its → moves 3px.
on the live site: the sheet plots once when 50% visible. Reduced motion shows the fully plotted final state.
notes: 1008px tall on the shared C metric: a 96px lead-in where the frame continues, the 384px title row (label y 120, title bottom y 422, rule y 450), a 480px body (spec head, four 60px rows, then the two 96px door cells on R8 and R9) and a 48px band. All geometry is generated (scratchpad caudit/gen_cta.py) so lines land on the frame and iso angles are exact. Because the plane spans the full footprint, its back half sits behind the lowest plates on screen in a true 30° view; the dashed projectors carry the height reading. Red: the sheet itself is the one full-red moment. The plane and audit door are its paper inversion, and the plan lines on the plane are red on paper. The coherence pass moved this sheet onto the shared head and band, fixed the numbering (13/14), redrew FIG. 13.1 with the corrected mark geometry, and removed a broken UTC clock.
